title: While Man City defend their past, PSG show they own the present in UCL - CBS Sports
description: Enzo Maresca's tactical gamble backfired and Gianluigi Donnarumma struggled in goal, leaving Pep Guardiola to wat
body:
Enzo Maresca's tactical gamble backfired and Gianluigi Donnarumma struggled in goal, leaving Pep Guardiola to watch his former side stumble
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:12 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There was an air of defiance about Manchester City, an arrogance that comes naturally to those who have developed a false sense of victimhood. Then again, they were not exactly wrong to boast some level of confidence – even if the Premier League found them guilty of 115 financial breaches, City had assembled a team that would at the very least contend in matches worth watching, even if the results could become invalidated in the not-too-distant future. City's supporters, Pep Guardiola included, filled Etihad Stadium on Wednesday with an expectation that the players on the pitch would not sour the mood, no matter that the guilty verdict suggests the collection of talent should not actually be there.Instead, what the stubborn onlookers got was a dose of reality.In some ways, it is not a surprise that back-to-back UEFA Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain would use Wednesday's game as another opportunity to assert their dominance with a 4-2 win. Their unique brand of dynamism is still a defining feature, one that is still hard to beat two years after manager Luis Enrique's tactical reinvention. Ousmane Dembele and Desire Doue are still impressively clinical, Vitinha still amongst the world's best in midfield. What was genuinely impressive, though, is that they were unflinching on a day that tested City's sporting construction.The hosts ultimately outshot PSG 27 to 15, racking up 2.5 expected goals while the European champions only tallied up 1.83. City's end product matched their efforts, Erling Haaland once again assuming cheat code mode with a brace that kept his side in the game while becoming the club's top goalscorer in the competition. Their defensive resolve failed the tests PSG posed time and time again on Wednesday, though, defined by a mistake-ridden performance from goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.The Italy international has always been a respectable option in goal but at 27 years old, he does not seem on pace to become one of his generation's top options. His inability to respond to Doue's opener in the 13th minute and Dembele's goal two minutes later was surprising, almost single-handedly digging his team into a hole they could barely dig themselves out of. It was a recurring theme over the course of 90 minutes, even as he saved Ferran Torres' tame penalty in the 90th minute.
Donnarumma was hardly the only person to blame for City's woes on Wednesday. Head coach Enzo Maresca opted to use Elliot Anderson as the lone player in midfield while just about everyone in front of him took a more advanced position, an imbalanced approach that was misguided from the start. It did not get the best out of anyone, PSG taking a 3-0 lead by halftime while City took just six shots and mustered 0.79 expected goals at that point.Maresca's halftime decision to bring on Ayyoub Bouaddi for Jeremy Doku and offer Anderson some assistance in midfield was to City's benefit but at that point, it was far too late. There was not much left to salvage despite a valiant effort, headlined by Haaland.Guardiola made a quick trip to Manchester to be a supportive figure but in the end, his shadow loomed large. The generous read of Maresca's tactical mistakes to start is that he borrowed Guardiola's famous overthinking habit for Wednesday's marquee matchup but in actuality, the new City boss does not have the reputation just yet to afford that kind of benefit of the doubt. Even then, Guardiola's ability to overthink was not the type of thing that would prevent someone from pointing out when he got something wrong and even if Maresca is the right successor, there is no reason to stop short of saying his choices were costly on Wednesday.
It was not the only way Guardiola's legacy hung over the Etihad, though. He receives a hero's welcome time and time again in that part of Manchester because he stewarded a superteam with his new position in the stands rather than on the pitch, the clearest sign as any that those days are a thing of the past. City's post-Guardiola rebuild means the team is still very much a work in progress, the team not favorites to win the biggest titles in front of them for the time being.It makes City fans' defiance all the more intriguing. While opposing fans expertly spent the prolonged international break successfully making Oasis puns to sell the point, a sign reading "What's the story? Tainted glory" at Anfield on Sunday, all City supporters could come up with was worship for club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. They have rallied around an executive and a series of businesspeople rather than the players on the pitch, all while erasing their actual case as victims – these are the very people who tarnished what should be the happiest sporting experiences, and ultimately what should be a storied chapter in the English game.The funniest part, though, is that for all of City's advantages, Guardiola's tenure looks more and more like magic in a bottle. Watching Donnarumma's slow response to Doue, another beneficiary of a nation-state's backing, it was hard not to ask: This is all City could come up with after all their efforts to work around the Premier League's financial systems?

title: Burning questions for Week 7: Can Notre Dame pass first test, is Texas broken? - CBS Sports
description: A number of questions will finally be answered during the biggest weekend on the college football calendar to dat
body:
A number of questions will finally be answered during the biggest weekend on the college football calendar to date
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It is officially spooky season, but for college football fans we're living in seventh heaven. The week is absolutely loaded across the sport, and it affords us the opportunity to continue to learn about teams.That's what mid-October should be all about: getting to know why teams are real and which aren't. The junk filters out as conference play gets going, and the buy games are a thing of the past. It's an important part of the calendar as the ramp-up to the first College Football Playoff rankings truly begins. And it's punctuated by weeks like this. Outside of Ohio State vs. Indiana, perhaps there isn't truly a marquee matchup, but there are important things to be found across the schedule outside of that mammoth top-10 matchup. But this is also where a key part of the discourse is built for the playoff race itself. The SEC teams you thought were really good because they were highly ranked in September? Well, they're about to start beating up on one another the deeper into conference play we get (Florida, Ole Miss, LSU on notice there).
So what does one do with that information? The SEC would like you to do what benefits them. Look carefully at how the narrative begins, and you'll surely see the parity throughout the next few weeks. Because their losses matter but yours don't. And their parity below the best teams matters, while yours doesn't (mostly looking at you, Big Ten). Those questions will linger throughout the next few weeks. So what questions get answered across the nation in Week 7? 
        
            
                Loyal to a fault: These 5 teams are paying the price for sticking with familiar faces in 2026
                
                    John Talty                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Ohio State vs. IndianaHow far off last year's pace are the Hoosiers, really? This is not the Indiana of last season. They've yet to showcase a true penchant for tearing decent teams limb from limb like they have the last few seasons. They beat Ohio State last year in the Big Ten Championship Game, but they come into this one after surviving a road test against Nebraska.Indiana's defensive front is fearsome, and Ohio State's own issues running the ball are expected to be laid bare, but with No. 4 in Scarlet and Gray, Indiana's back seven risks being significantly exposed. Curt Cignetti called Jeremiah Smith a freak earlier this week. The game is at home, which should help the Hoosiers, but don't count on busts to bail out the Indiana passing game like the Cornhuskers so kindly gave IU last week. Can they stay efficient down-to-down, or will Josh Hoover's turnovers rear their ugly head?

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Florida vs. TexasWhat's really wrong with Texas' offense?  Arch Manning gets the headlines, and the issues typically fall at the quarterback's feet on offense, but there are more underlying concerns that are at the bedrock of Texas's offense. To get where the Longhorns want to go, they have to run the ball more efficiently than they are right now on early downs (first and second down). According to TruMedia, Texas ranks 110th in stuff percentages on running back runs among teams when filtering to FBS competition only.Overall, their numbers for stuff rate, EPA per rush, yards before contact, and yards after contact are simply woeful. They're 88th in rushing yards per game and 117th in yards per rush. They are simply stuck in the mud with a down-to-down drive efficiency rate because they can't run the ball, and it's giving the passing game no help. A lot of resources went into Texas' rushing attack this season, in the form of Hollywood Smothers and Raleek Brown.If Texas can run the ball better against the Gators, and they might, because Florida's defense has shown it is not up to the task in many ways this season, it could be the get-right game UT needs to quiet the noise, if only for a week.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Alabama vs. TennesseeHow much of a limiting factor is the Vols' QB situation? The uniforms will be neutral, but will Tennessee bring its offense to the party to match the sartorial success? The quarterback conundrum continues out of Knoxville, and it remains to be seen what George MacIntyre can do for the Vols if he's QB1. The early returns against a bad Arkansas team last week did not exactly leave much room for optimism. Bama went shot for shot with Georgia and came out on the wrong end of the scoreboard [Insert acknowledging the bad pass interference call]. How does Alabama put that behind them for the rivalry tilt?
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Missouri vs. Ole MissDid the Rebels actually fix that defense in the bye week?Welcome back home, Austin Simmons. With plenty of players and coaches on the other sideline that Simmons is familiar with, how does the return home go for the former Rebel? He's downplaying it, of course, but it will always matter. One of the most important things about the matchup is how Ole Miss' defense stands up against Missouri. Simmons is fun as a passer, but Mizzou wants to do one thing first and foremost: pound the rock. With a zone run scheme that hasn't missed a beat in Ahmad Hardy's unfortunate absence, as the emergence of Jamal Roberts comes to the forefront, Florida tore apart the Rebels' run D. For Missouri's own tremendous run defense, how does it stand up to Ole Miss' rushing attack, which has Kewan Lacy back, theoretically much closer to full strength than he was last week?

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. UCLA vs. WisconsinDoes the QB injury matter? Nico Iamaleava is likely out for the season, and it's not clear exactly how much that will affect UCLA's offense. This is not a team that has been getting the job done with a particularly prolific passing game. In fact, only 12 teams in the country pass at a lower clip than the Bruins, and three of them are the service academies. What does Ty Dieffenbach have as the Bruins face a surprisingly good Wisconsin defense, which has found its form mainly by short-circuiting opponents' passing attacks?
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Oklahoma State vs. HoustonIs the loser out of the Big 12 race? Don't let this game fly under the radar because this is a really cool Big 12 gut check. On paper, both teams are evenly matched. Both offenses are good. Both defenses are a little less so, but this is one of the two or three most important games in deciding the Big 12 race overall, as both of these two teams seem primed to take a spot in Arlington, Texas, if either BYU or Texas Tech falters. Oklahoma State does not play BYU, but gets Tech on Nov. 18. Houston lost to Tech, but doesn't play BYU either. The conference race will be crowded, and this will be one we point back to at season's end that helped decide it.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Notre Dame vs. BYUWhat happens when the Irish are properly tested? Welcome to the party, Notre Dame. The Irish have seemingly taken the last five weeks off since their game against Wisconsin. If you'd forgotten about them, you would certainly be forgiven.
Heading into the season, it was clear Notre Dame's season would more or less boil down to two games: this one and Miami on Nov. 7. If they lose this game, their margin of error vaporizes, and the Miami game becomes a binary exercise for playoff inclusion, for all intents and purposes. Notre Dame found out the hard way what the downsides of a soft schedule are in their specific independent case and that one posed much tougher tests than this one did. BYU will be without its best player, LJ Martin, and, so far this season, has been missing a truly explosive element in the passing game. Playing Notre Dame when you're anything approaching one-dimensional is not a recipe for success.

title: Cowboys' Joey Porter Jr. breaks silence after missing Week 5 game - CBS Sports
description: FRISCO, Texas -- New Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. knew he was in trouble on Thursday morning, the day of his new team's "Th
body:
FRISCO, Texas -- New Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. knew he was in trouble on Thursday morning, the day of his new team's "Thursday Night Football" showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Porter Jr., who the Cowboys acquired in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick, played on 48.1% (25 of 52) of the Cowboys' defensive snaps in their 34-30 road win over the Houston Texans. He and the team were ramping up for him to be a full-time starter after being on the roster for a week, but those plans changed quickly when he woke up that day. He had an itchy throat in the morning, and that feeling stuck with him during morning walkthroughs with his Cowboys teammates. Porter Jr. reported feeling ill to the team, and they gave him cold medicine to deal with his symptoms. By the time it was time to drive down from Frisco, where Dallas' team facility is located, to Arlington, where AT&T Stadium is just over 35 miles down the road, Porter Jr. was ready to vomit. He told his Uber driver to floor it to the stadium, so that he could go ahead and vomit when he arrived. That's when he and the team knew he wouldn't be suiting up Thursday night. "I really just couldn't hold anything down. I just kept throwing up," Porter Jr. said Wednesday after practice, his first media availability since the illness. "I tried to fight through it. I tried taking a nap before the game to shake it off, but I couldn't hold anything down. That's when they made the call to send me home. ... Throughout the day, it just kept getting worse and worse. On my way to the game when I was throwing up outside of my Uber on the way to the game, it was brutal. Not going to lie."
Week 5 was supposed to be Porter Jr.'s home opener against a winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers team starting Jalon Daniels, an undrafted rookie making his second career start. A happy coronation in front of his new home fans was all lined up. Instead, Porter Jr. ended up watching Dallas lose from home in a shocking 24-16 defeat. "It was very frustrating. I was prepared to play all week. The mind was playing. The mindset was to get the dub," Porter Jr. said. "Obviously, I didn't get to do that, and we didn't get the dub. I was pretty pissed in my couple days off."Not that it excuses Dallas' poor performance, particularly on defense where they allowed a whopping 241 yards rushing, but Thursday was the Cowboys' third game in 12 days. That stretch also included two 10-hour flights from Dallas to Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. They were all worn out. Energy is much higher around the locker room, especially from Porter Jr., with a 10-day gap between Thursday and their "Sunday Night Football" matchup at the Green Bay Packers (3-2) in Week 6. The layoff especially helped Porter, who will now have been a Cowboy for 17 days before he takes the field with a higher workload. 
"I feel great. Those extra days definitely helped. Helped me lock in with the playbook too. It was win-win. I was mad I couldn't be out there with the guys on that Thursday night," Porter Jr. said. "I was beating myself up, and my dad was just telling me 'keep the main thing the main thing and focus on what we have ahead of us.' That's Green Bay." Porter Jr.'s Packers outlookWith a higher comfort with the Cowboys' playbook, does that mean Porter Jr. will be a full-time starter on Sunday? Yes, yes, it does. "Definitely," he said with a soft smile. "That's what I'm shooting for, and that's what they're [the coaching staff] shooting for as well, so that's what we're going to try to do."
His return is crucial for a Dallas secondary that has the highest opposing passer rating (120.5) in the entire league entering Week 6. Especially since the Green Bay Packers' passing attack is full steam ahead after a 31-7 Week 5 demolition of the Chicago Bears on Sunday. Quarterback Jordan Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, with much of his damage coming in explosive play chunks. He went big-game hunting over and over to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches). That made Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016.  Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). He connected with Golden on throws of 36 yards and 50 yards. According to ESPN Insights, Love joined Ben Roethlisberger as the only players with five completions of 30-plus air yards in a game since ESPN began tracking the metric 20 years ago in 2006. However, Porter Jr. sees Love's eagerness to let it rip downfield as an opportunity for him and a Cowboys defense that has gone three consecutive games without a takeaway, one game away from the longest streak in team history. Dallas is the only team in the NFL without an interception this season. 
"I see that we have a lot of opportunities to make plays on the ball, so I know we're all excited for that," Porter Jr. said. "We really have to rally to the ball and make plays when they call on us to."Cowboys edge rusher Rashan Gary, the Packers' 2019 first-round pick the year before Green Bay used their next one on Love in 2020, spent six of his seven seasons with the Packers practicing against Love every day. He's making sure his teammates have a healthy respect for the 27-year-old quarterback, now in his fourth year as an NFL starter. "Swagger, confidence, his poise. Understanding defensive ID. Understanding the nickel's rotation. Understanding the coverage he is getting in the back. Able to find a way to get his playmakers the ball. A guy that is relentless," Gary said Wednesday. "A guy that wants to throw the ball, but if his lane is open, he will scramble. Just a true winner." 
It will be interesting to see how much Love tries to go Porter Jr.'s way. In his Dallas debut against the Texans, Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud didn't target Porter Jr. during his 19 coverage snaps. "It's a respect thing. That's how I look at it at the end of the day. If I'm not getting any work, that's the beautiful thing about defense," Porter Jr. "You can find your own work. If they're not looking toward you, that's when you need to get in the run game and show your presence. ... It can never be boring. There's always work out there. That's what I look forward to."Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked total defense (395.4 total yards per game allowed), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed), and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it. That's why they hired former Cleveland Browns head coach and Packers defensive coordinator Mike Pettine this week as a senior assistant to first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Porter Jr. sees that move and the decision to trade for him as investments in winning. 
"It just shows that we're trying to get things done the right way, and we're trying to win. That's the main thing that everyone is focused on, to win," Porter Jr. said. "When you have guys all willing and able to put into the pile, that's when good things happen. That's what we're looking forward to."So when will four steady quarters of action come for the Cowboys? They led the Buccaneers 10-7 before the meltdown occurred in the second half. Maybe Week 6 is the time. "It's right there. We all watch the tape. We all know what we need to work on," Porter Jr. said. "It's a couple plays that are holding us back. If we just do what we need to do, those plays and those little miscues should be cleaned up."

title: Lakers' JJ Redick on Bronny James: 'I don't think he's played well' - CBS Sports
description: Bronny has struggled this preseason, combining for 11 points and 12 turnovers in four games
body:
Bronny has struggled this preseason, combining for 11 points and 12 turnovers in four games
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:33 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Through the Lakers' first four preseason games, guard Bronny James hasn't been able to find a rhythm. James, who is entering Year 3 of his NBA career and playing his first season without his father, LeBron James, on the same team, has 11 points and 12 turnovers combined in the preseason.In the Lakers' 101-89 loss to the Warriors on Wednesday in Las Vegas, James went scoreless in 11 minutes of action. James attempted just two shots and finished with one rebound, one steal and four turnovers. After the game, Lakers coach JJ Redick said James hasn't "played well" in the Lakers' preseason games but has had good practices leading up to the preseason."I thought he had a really nice September and a good summer with us, but I don't think he's played well in the four preseason games, but he's had good practices," Redick said. "Again, some of it is just rhythm, some of it is who he's playing with. He's played a lot of minutes, especially in the second half of games with our two-way guys. Tonight he played with Rafael (Castro), who has been with us for three days. Some of it is like the group he's with. I think that is not necessarily setting him up for success."
The Lakers guaranteed James' deal for the 2026-27 season at $2.29 million earlier this summer as part of the four-year, $7.89 million contract he signed after being selected with the No. 55 overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft. Heading into this summer, only $1.25 million of the $2.29 million salary was guaranteed. The Lakers currently have 16 players on their active roster and will have to trim it down at least one spot ahead of cutdown day on Monday. Los Angeles has one final preseason game against the Nuggets on Friday before opening the regular season at home against the Warriors on Oct. 21.After playing 27 regular-season games in 2024-25, James appeared in 42 last season. The younger James also split time with the South Bay Lakers (now the Coachella Valley Lakers), the team's G League affiliate. James shot 38.6% from the 3-point line (on 1.4 attempts per game) and earned playoff minutes throughout the first round against the Rockets.
However, heading into Year 3, it's unclear what his role looks like. Lakers star Luka Dončić didn't play against the Warriors on Wednesday, but Redick still played 16 different players, with James logging 11 minutes off the bench.

title: Joe Brady reveals what Bills should have done differently in overtime vs. Rams - CBS Sports
description: Brady said Buffalo could have taken two knees before Tyler Bass' winning field goal, limiting the Rams' opportuni
body:
Brady said Buffalo could have taken two knees before Tyler Bass' winning field goal, limiting the Rams' opportunity to answer if the kick missed
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In a week dominated by coaching gaffes and clock mismanagement, the victors are trying to learn from their counterparts' mistakes. There were some missteps that went unnoticed, however. Such as one from Joe Brady of the Buffalo Bills. Brady's Bills scored a massive, 37-34 victory over the Los Angeles Rams in overtime, but the first-year lead man identified one area where he could have been better. After Buffalo tipped Harrison Mevis' 48-yard field goal attempt in the extra period, the Bills marched 35 yards down the field on five plays and set up Tyler Bass for a game-winning 45-yard field goal with 1:55 remaining on a second-and-10. Brady now wishes he had called a couple of kneel-downs to take some time off the clock and cover his bases if Bass happened to miss his kick as Mevis did."I didn't want to run two QB sneaks with the thought process of putting the ball in harm's way, taking some shots on Josh, just to get — we knew we were already in line," Brady said. "So it's like, hey, do I just, hey, center the ball and just take two knees? You know, you go back two yards, but you don't give them, you know, they end up worse if you miss. They get 45 seconds to go 20 yards for the field goal. Big difference in two-minute, and the 45-yard field goal and a 47-yard field goal percentages, you should still be good to go.
"So if I had that opportunity again — look, I was conflicted about it. You know, T-Bass was good to go. The conversation we had in the huddle and upstairs was like, 'Let's just go win the game right now.' But to not give them that shot again if we do miss, the best thing would be is to take two knees and say, 'Hey, the 45 and the 47 is not of big difference.' Be a completely different story if the ball was a little further back. I'd be no indecision on taking knees if we were a little closer. We were just in that is a long field goal, we had just missed an extra point, but had the confidence in T-Bass, but that's one I do wish I probably took two knees and then we kick the game winner. And if anything, they'd have 45 seconds and not two minutes."
Running down the clock in overtime is something every NFL team needs to consider -- as long as you don't pull a Washington Commanders and run out the clock on yourself. But something else for NFL teams to consider is remaining aggressive in overtime. The Bills didn't have to kick a 45-yard field goal on second-and-10. They could have continued to gain yardage, run the clock and set up Bass for an easier field goal. 
It would have been pretty embarrassing if Bass, who missed an extra point in the third quarter, had missed his 45-yard field goal on second down and allowed Matthew Stafford to engineer a game-winning drive with 1:50 remaining on the clock.

title: Rory McIlroy says Tommy Fleetwood inspired his new baggy pants look, but it's 'a work in progress' - CBS Sports
description: McIlroy surprised many by showing up to India with wide le
body:
McIlroy surprised many by showing up to India with wide leg pants and says he didn't bring a backup option
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:14 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Professional golfers are always looking at their peers for things they can incorporate into their games. Wander the range before a PGA Tour event and you'll see guys peeking in bags, checking out different clubs and seeing what all their competitors are doing to gain an advantage. For Rory McIlroy, it's not just equipment that he's had an eye on this year from his fellow PGA Tour pros. McIlroy turned heads when he showed up at the DP World India Championship this week in baggy pants, and video of his new look went viral on social media. McIlroy was asked about the new look in a TV interview and admitted that he's "watched and admired Tommy Fleetwood" and his shift to baggy pants this year, so he decided to give it a shot. 
McIlroy, who typically wears a more fitted, tapered pant on the golf course, notes that in his everyday life he has embraced the wide-leg trend and has been inspired by his buddy Fleetwood to give it a try. 
Nick Faldo had a number of questions, including a key question about whether McIlroy had any backups of his usual trousers in case he decided he didn't like the feel of the new pants on the course. McIlroy admitted he didn't pack anything else for his trip to India, and also said he's not totally happy with the fit of what he brought. He said they sit a bit low and are a little shorter than he's used to, calling it a "work in progress," which is an objectively funny thing to say about changing the pants you wear to play golf.
Faldo's concern is that McIlroy's pants could be a distraction if they feel different on the golf course, as any thought about your pants takes focus away from executing a shot. McIlroy is hoping to facilitate some additional air flow in hot, humid New Delhi, and at the very least, if McIlroy struggles this week in India, there will be a built-in excuse in the form of his new pants.

title: NFL addresses safety concerns for Steelers-Saints game in France protests in Paris continues - CBS Sports
description: The league says it is still planning to play the game as originally scheduled
body:
The league says it is still planning to play the game as originally scheduled
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With protests on their third week in Paris and an NFL game scheduled to take place in the city in just 11 days, growing concern over fan and player safety has left some wondering if the league will alter any of its plans. But the NFL said on Wednesday that the game will go on as scheduled, with the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints meeting on Oct. 25 at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, located just north of Paris."We're excited for the first-ever regular season game in Paris, and preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France on October 25," the NFL said in a statement, via ESPN. "As we do for every NFL game, including our international games, we work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month."The social unrest stems from demands for the government to change multiple aspects of the education system. Protestors are asking the government to address under-resourced schools, poor conditions and teacher shortages. Students say the schools are falling apart and rats are in the buildings. The protests have sparked violence, with authorities using tear gas, stun grenades and various other means to attempt to stop the crowds. Protestors have reportedly set fires and caused damage. Police detained over 5,000 people in connection with protests, according to CBS News. 
Local officials say they are investigating both the protests and the police response. The French government is currently in a "political deadlock" as they approach the presidential elections in the spring. They have not responded to protestors with any plans or solutions for their complaints and demands. If the situation in Paris escalates, the NFL could reconsider its stance, but right now, it is sticking with its original plan. The NFL has changed game locations in the past due to extreme weather or field conditions. 
The Saints are considered the home team for the game, and their only listed event for the day in New Orleans is a private event where youth and amateur sports teams have the chance to play inside the stadium. It is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. local time, so if needed, the game could seemingly be played at Caesar's Superdome. But that seems unlikely at the moment.If the game does go on as planned, it will mark the first-ever NFL game played in France.  This will be the second straight year the Steelers play a game outside the United States, having played in Dublin last season against the Minnesota Vikings. The Saints last played an international game in 2022, visiting London to face the Vikings.

title: Agent's Take: Making sense of Eagles' salary cap manipulation after Lane Johnson's sudden retirement - CBS Sports
description: The Eagles kept Johnson on their 53-man roster after his abrupt Week 5 retirement. Here's a look at why and what
body:
The Eagles kept Johnson on their 53-man roster after his abrupt Week 5 retirement. Here's a look at why and what they gain from it
        
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    
            
    
        Philadelphia Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson abruptly retired due to personal reasons a couple of days after he was a surprise inactive for Week 4's contest against the Los Angeles Rams. The expectation was that the Eagles would put Johnson on the reserve/retired list because of his decision. Instead, the Eagles, who have suffered a rash of injuries, are reportedly going to keep Johnson on the 53-man roster. The roster decision is for salary cap reasons and also allows Johnson to change his mind about playing at some point this season, which seems unlikely. Johnson cited focusing on his mental health as a primary reason for his retirement in a statement he posted on his Instagram page.Johnson is making $23 million this year, consisting of a $1.3 million base salary and a $21.7 million option bonus. Half of the option bonus, or $10.85 million, has already been paid. The remaining $10.85 million is payable on December 1.Option bonuses are prorated on a team's salary cap over the life of a contract (including the option years and up to a maximum of five years) beginning in the league year when the option is exercised. This means Johnson's $21.7 million is prorated on Philadelphia's salary cap at $4.34 million annually from 2026 through 2030.
I suspect the Eagles wouldn't have hesitated to put Johnson on the retired list if the entire $23 million had been base salary. In that case, Johnson would be forfeiting roughly $17.9 million (14/18ths of $23 million), which would have come as salary cap relief for the Eagles in 2026.How NFL teams view retirementRetiring would typically put Johnson in breach of his contract, giving the Eagles the right to recoup money from him. Under the NFL collective bargaining agreement, an option bonus is only forfeitable if a breach occurs in the league year where the money is earned. Keeping Johnson on the 53-man roster means the Eagles won't be able to declare he is in breach and recover some of the 2026 option bonus. The Eagles don't have any recovery rights to Johnson's $18.79 million 2024 option bonus and $23.745 million 2025 option bonus because no breach occurred in either year.The recoupment standard is different for signing bonuses. A team has a right to recover the prorated amount of a signing bonus in the current and future years of a contract when a player retires. The $18.835 million signing bonus Johnson received in 2023 still has $3.767 million prorated in 2026 and 2027 for salary cap purposes.
Some NFL teams are reluctant to enforce these rights, especially for a player with a Hall of Fame-worthy career like Johnson. (Though that didn't stop the San Francisco 49ers from getting money back from Hall of Fame linebacker Patrick Willis when he prematurely retired in 2015 after eight NFL seasons, according to a conversation I had with a 49ers front office executive a few years ago.)If the Eagles processed Johnson's retirement in 2026 (when recoupment isn't pursued), they would have $42.89 million of 2027 dead money — a salary cap charge for a player no longer on a team's roster — from the bonus proration in Johnson's 2027 through 2030 contract years. Here's what the dead money would consist of:$3.767 million prorated from his $18.835 million signing bonus in 2023 relating to Johnson's 2027 contract year$7.516 million prorated from his $18.79 million option bonus in 2024 relating to his 2027 and 2028 contract years$14.247 million prorated from his $23.745 million option bonus in 2025 relating to his 2027 through 2029 contract years$17.36 million prorated from the $21.7 million option bonus relating to his 2027 through 2029 contract years, as well as a dummy/voiding 2030 contract yearThe $42.89 million would be $18.06 million more than Johnson's listed 2027 cap of $24.83 million. Johnson would be off Philadelphia's books beginning in 2028.
So what's the Eagles' plan? The plan is for the Eagles to delay processing Johnson's retirement until next June 2 at the earliest. That's because only the current year's bonus proration counts toward the salary cap with players released, traded or retiring after June 1. The prorated bonus in future contract years is delayed until the following league year, which typically begins in early to mid-March. By waiting so long to list Johnson as retired, this $42.89 million will be split into $16.614 million of dead money in 2027 and $26.276 million of dead money in 2028. That's likely what the Eagles were already planning for with Johnson previously stating 2026 would probably be his final season. In this scenario, Johnson's 2027 dead money is $8.216 million less than his current 2027 cap number.The $16.614 million will be the 2027 prorated amount from Johnson's 2023 signing bonus and his three option bonuses from 2024, 2025 and 2026. The $26.276 million will be the prorated amount from the three option bonuses in the next three years of Johnson's contract.
How Johnson's situation compares to othersTeams have delayed retirement processing before, but not quite to this extreme. For example, after Hall of Fame quarterback Drew Brees announced his retirement in March 2021, the New Orleans Saints kept him on the roster until June 11 because waiting was more advantageous from a salary cap standpoint.There is speculation that the Eagles and Johnson's camp will work out how much of the 2026 option bonus will be retained, given his roster status. It wouldn't be surprising if the $10.85 million Johnson is due in December isn't paid. The Saints and Derek Carr did something similar when the quarterback unexpectedly retired in May 2025 with an injured right shoulder. Carr kept the $10 million roster bonus for 2025 that he had already received. He forfeited the other $30 million he was scheduled to make in 2025, of which $28.745 million had been converted into a signing bonus for cap purposes. The Saints waived rights to $17.1 million of a 2023 signing bonus that was subject to recoupment due to his retirement.
For the Eagles, it remains to be seen how any potential savings from the 2026 option bonus would be treated under the salary cap. It's conceivable the savings would be applied proportionately. This would mean the 2026 through 2030 option bonus proration would be reduced by $2.17 million annually if the $10.85 million December payment isn't made. Under this scenario, there would be $34.21 million of 2027 dead money split into $14.444 million next year and $19.766 million in 2028.

schema.headline: Agent's Take: Making sense of Eagles' salary cap manipulation after Lane Johnson's sudden retirement - CBS Sports

title: Warriors' Kristaps Porziņģis breaks silence on mysterious health issues - CBS Sports
description: Porziņģis also tried to quiet some of the online rumors that have circulated about his absence from the court
body:
Porziņģis also tried to quiet some of the online rumors that have circulated about his absence from the court
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Golden State Warriors will begin the season without one of their expected key contributors as Kristaps Porzingis will remain sidelined indefinitely due to an unspecified health issue. Porziņģis, who signed a two-year, $40 million deal in the offseason, missed the entirety of training camp and all of their preseason games to this point, but returned to the Warriors facility for the first time this fall on Tuesday. Porziņģis and the Warriors each released statements on Wednesday offering a vague update on his status going forward. Porziņģis, 31, posted to social media that he's been working with doctors and is "getting better and better," but is still not ready to return to the court and must remain patient."Hello people, I'm working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health asap. Honestly, I'm getting better and better. I just have to stay patient, and I believe I'll be feeling great again soon," Porziņģis wrote. "It has definitely been frustrating dealing with some health stuff that you can't exactly pinpoint, on top of injuries throughout my career, so it has added up for sure, but we will get through it. Health is wealth. Thank you for all the support."He followed that up by speaking directly to the "internet doctors" who have been trying to diagnose him and tried to quiet some of the rumors about his condition. 
The Warriors said that Porziņģis met with general manager Mike Dunleavy and vice president of player health and performance Dr. Rick Celebrini upon his return to the team practice facility on Tuesday. The team did not provide a timeline for Porziņģis' potential return and said the "specific contents of that meeting will remain private.""Porziņģis will remain out indefinitely due to the same health-related matter but will be around the team," the Warriors said. "An update on his status, including the potential resumption of practice, playing status or timeline, will be provided when available and appropriate."
The Warriors added Porziņģis in a deal with the Atlanta Hawks ahead of last year's trade deadline. He played in 15 games for Golden State, averaging 16.1 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.3 assists. The No. 4 pick in the 2015 NBA Draft, Porziņģis has dealt with health and injury issues throughout his career. While knee injuries were a common problem earlier in his career, various mysterious health issues have persisted in recent seasons. During his time with the Boston Celtics, Porziņģis was sidelined while experiencing fatigue and was later diagnosed with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS), which can cause rapid changes in heart rate, exhaustion and dizziness. 
Porziņģis was expected to take on a major role this season for the Warriors and being around the team seems like a step in the right direction. Still, until he's able to return, the Warriors' frontcourt rotation will be a bit thinner than initially planned. Al Horford and Charles Bassey are the other center options on the roster beyond Draymond Green, and the Warriors figure to play some small-ball lineups that could incorporate rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who has impressed in the preseason, at the four spot.

title: No place like Rome: Mourinho gets UCL comeback win for Real Madrid and the last laugh - CBS Sports
description: The Portuguese boss faced off with his former employers and broke hearts with a wild comeback win
body:
The Portuguese boss faced off with his former employers and broke hearts with a wild comeback win
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        ROME -- There is no place like Rome, and if you're Jose Mourinho, it can get even better. It was an emotional night at the Stadio Olimpico as AS Roma welcomed Real Madrid and their former coach and lost 4-3 to the Spanish giants at the end of a crazy second half, when AS Roma were up 3-1 until the 83rd minute before conceding three goals in the last seven minutes with three corner kicks and the goals of Carlos Espi, Endrick and Toni Rudiger. Roma fans left the stadium softly chanting after losing their first match back at the Stadio Olimpico seven years after playing their last home game in the top European tournament. Mourinho, on the other hand, seemed particularly happy to win but was also received as a hero by his former fans. For the Portuguese coach, this is a statement win. He replaced players such as Vinicius Jr., Yan Diomande, Denzel Dumfries in the second half and won on his own terms. At the final whistle, he left the pitch pointing a finger at the sky: it was a crazy win, and it was also his night, defeating the club that he led to UEFA Conference League glory just over four years ago.
Gian Piero Gasperini, the current AS Roma coach, was basically the one who ended the stint of Mourinho at the Italian club, as the defeat against Atalanta that took place in January 2024 convinced American businessman and AS Roma owner Dan Friedkin to sack the Portuguese coach three years after shocking the world by appointing him. Two years later, the world is different in Rome. Gasperini is convincing week after week that he's the right coach in the right place but the defeat against Real Madrid is another signal that they shouldn't consider themselves at the level of the top European teams yet. With all the issues of Real Madrid that need to be taken into account, it was a moment of revelation for Gasperini and his team until the 83rd minute, before the mistakes of the Italian defense and the quality of the Real Madrid players took over. Until then, everything was just perfect: the performance and the players who scored the three AS Roma goals are a reflection of that. Marten De Roon, the Dutch midfielder that Gasperini had at Atalanta and brought to Rome this summer, opened the score, followed by Danyell Malen's brace, the most crucial signing that AS Roma made in recent years. But in the end, more than anything, it was mainly the night of Mourinho, as he made his comeback in the city for the first time since his sacking in 2024. A place that loved him like few before, and welcomed him with respect and admiration, the same feelings they showed to him when he was on the Roma bench were existent on Wednesday night.
In the first moments of the game, Mourinho didn't seek attention; he didn't need it. He spoke nicely about his former team before the game but he knew something would happen on Wednesday. All eyes were on him, even when he hadn't arrived to the bench. When the speaker announced the lineups, before naming the Real Madrid players, he welcomed "The Special One" who managed the club from 2021 to 2024, winning the UEFA Conference League, the first UEFA trophy in the history of the club, and losing the UEFA Europa League final one year later. 
The whole stadium applauded him and the AS Roma pre-match routine took place: the Champions League anthem, the emotional Roma anthem and then it was time for Mourinho again, a few minutes into the match. Roma's Curva Sud wrote on a banner, "Who brings glory to Rome, Rome honors forever. Your hands are blessed and the people tribute you eternal glory," followed by his name chanted by the whole Olimpico and more banners and pictures of him were shown afterwards by the fans. Mourinho sent kisses back, showing his love and appreciation to a place where he is more than a hero.It seemed a terrible night at one point when Roma were up 3-1, but the epic end of the match just made everything better for him in traditional Real Madrid fashion. 
He'll never admit it, but there must be a special satisfaction in beating the team and owners who sacked him two years earlier. He made a similar point about Chelsea and his former boss, Roman Abramovich, in a recent Netflix documentary. The bond between him and Roma fans runs deep, and their love for him seems eternal. In soccer, nothing lasts forever: results shape the fortunes of players and managers, and even the strongest relationships can fade with time. But Mourinho holds a special place in the hearts of Roma fans, and that affection will never fade, even after wins like these.

title: Vinicius Jr. set to miss El Clasico for Real Madrid after four match ban - CBS Sports
description: The Brazilian winger was sent off during the last home gam
body:
The Brazilian winger was sent off during the last home game against Villarreal after pulling Nathan Saliba's hair before scoring
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:54 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr. will miss El Clasico against FC Barcelona on Oct. 25 after being suspended for four games for the red card he received in Real Madrid's last home game, against Villarreal at the Bernabeu. The Brazilian forward came on in the 52nd minute and was sent off 20 minutes later. Vinicius Jr. thought he had scored, and Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho celebrated alongside his team and ran over to him a few seconds before VAR ruled out the goal and sent him off. The VAR check showed Vinicius Jr. had pulled Nathan Saliba's hair before scoring.  The Spanish Football Federation's rules state that pulling an opponent's hair is violent conduct, and Vinicius was suspended for the upcoming four Real Madrid matches against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia. The federation's competition committee gave Vinicius a two-game ban for "violent conduct, without the possibility of playing the ball" and two additional games "for arguing with the referee with an aggressive attitude and having to be restrained by his teammates."  Mourinho, who skipped Saturday's post-match press conference after the episode, spoke ahead of the Champions League match against AS Roma on Wednesday and said, "After the previous match against Atletico Madrid in which Vinicius started, I decided to take a different approach and to protect him a little and then bring him on when the game called for a player like Vini. I think that worked out well: the stadium, which had sometimes voiced disapproval, immediately rallied behind him the moment he started warming up. I believe that was a crucial turning point for him. He came on and played very well, the goal and the sending off were a shame, of course, but it seemed like something clicked for him, reigniting that joy and reminding him of the kind of player he truly is."  The ban applies only to domestic competitions, so Vinicius will be able to play against AS Roma on Wednesday, then against RB Leipzig and on Nov. 4 against AEK Athens. He will be eligible to play in LaLiga again only after the November international break, when Real Madrid meet Celta Vigo on Nov. 22.

        Help is on the way for the New England Patriots offense. Head coach Mike Vrabel announced that the team has opened up the practice window for receiver A.J. Brown, and he will be on the field on Wednesday. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in the team's season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks, which landed him on injured reserve. Week 6 was the earliest that Brown could be activated from IR, so the fact that he's able to get back to practice at this juncture is a positive sign that the ankle has healed at a good pace. "I don't know. He hasn't been out there," said Vrabel when asked what Brown's looming return means for the offense. "I can't tell you until we actually see it. He hadn't been out there for four weeks, so we'll get him back out there practicing and see if he's ready to go in a couple days. If not, then 21-day window and we'll go from there." 
New England will now have 21 days to move Brown onto the active roster, or else he'll revert back to injured reserve for the rest of the season. That said, it feels unlikely it'll take that long for him to eventually make his way back onto the 53-man roster and on the field. 
"I think he's stayed engaged," Vrabel said of how Brown has dealt with being injured. "I think it's difficult sometimes to stay engaged, but I think his routine was really good. His ability to be around the guys in meetings and also focus on his rehab. Just treated everything as a pro and be where he's supposed to be and work hard to get back." While it's unclear if Brown will be ready to go for the club's Week 6 matchup against the New York Jets, there is a wrinkle in the team's schedule worth pointing out. After this home matchup with the Jets, New England has a short week as they'll take on the Bears in Chicago on "Thursday Night Football" to begin Week 7. Given the tight turnaround, it's fair to wonder whether the Patriots will play it slow with Brown, with an eye for him to return for that game. "We obviously know we have a shortened week next week," said Vrabel. "Can't impact our decisions to try and do everything we can to win this week, and then figure out where we are after that." 
Brown was acquired in a blockbuster trade with the Eagles this offseason. New England shipped a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick to Philadelphia in exchange for the star pass catcher. On top of giving the Patriots a top-tier weapon, the trade also reunited Brown with Vrabel, who coached him when he first entered the league as a second-round pick of the Tennessee Titans in 2019.Last season for the Eagles, Brown caught 78 balls for 1,003 yards and seven touchdowns. In his brief showing with the Patriots in Week 1, the 29-year-old caught three of his four targets for 26 yards. Drake Maye will only improve with A.J. Brown back

title: Should Arch Manning return to Texas? Examining his 2027 NFL Draft decision - CBS Sports
description: For most of his football career, the question surrounding Arch Manning was when he'd enter the NFL Draft, not whether he would be ready
body:
For most of his football career, the question surrounding Arch Manning was when he'd enter the NFL Draft, not whether he would be ready once he got there. But five games into the 2026 season, we're having the same conversation we had midway through 2025: should he spend another year at Texas?Coach Steve Sarkisian said in June that he "wouldn't be surprised" if Manning returned for a fifth season in 2027. Earlier this month, uncle Eli Manning told Colin Cowherd that there's value in the college experience beyond simply preparing for the NFL, including opportunities to develop as a quarterback and leader.There has been no formal announcement, but the possibility raises a question worth exploring (again): Could one more year in college transform Manning into the top-five pick we've been hearing about, this time in the 2028 NFL Draft?He turns 23 in the spring, but despite four years in college, Manning has made just 20 career starts. He could finish 2026 with 27-30, and another season would push him toward 40. The question then becomes: would the additional games make a meaningful difference? History offers reasons for optimism, along with some warnings.
What Arch has shown, and what's missingAs discussed repeatedly, Manning's physical talent isn't the problem. He has a big arm, he navigates the pocket as well as anyone in the class, can excel off-platform and is an asset in the run game. And despite the uneven performances, he's quietly one of the better deep-ball throwers in this quarterback class.Through five games, Manning has a 93.1 PFF passing grade on throws traveling at least 20 yards, with 10 big-time throws on 24 attempts. He's completed only nine, but drops and circumstances matter. The tape routinely shows a quarterback who can throw with touch, drive and accuracy downfield.The problems pop up elsewhere, particularly when his first read isn't available.Manning can play hurried, at times, in clean pockets. It affects his footwork, accuracy and field vision. He'll skip reads, and there are stretches when he appears to see only part of the field.
Saturday's 27-24 loss to Oklahoma again offered both versions of Manning. He looked like the best player on the field on his 41-yard touchdown throw to Cam Coleman.
He had another big-boy touchdown toss to Ryan Wingo later in the game. And this laser to Coleman might be the best throw of his career:
But two fourth-quarter interceptions brought it all crashing back down to earth, again highlighting the decision-making and accuracy issues we've discussed for 14 months. It's why, even before the loss to Oklahoma, I had dropped Manning from my first mock draft of the fall. (Last year, I first dropped Manning from my mock draft in early November, a month before he announced his return to school.)
The fifth-year quarterbacks who made the leapThe encouraging news is that quarterbacks have made substantial improvements when returning to school for Year 5.Jayden Daniels entered his fifth season with more than 40 career starts. We all knew who he was athletically; he just needed to be more consistent as a passer. In his final season at LSU in 2023, his PFF passing grade jumped from 79.1 to 92.0, his big-time throw rate nearly tripled and his pressure-to-sack rate fell from 30.8% to 20.2%, suggesting better pocket awareness and decision-making under pressure.Daniels won the Heisman Trophy, was the No. 2 overall pick in 2024 and immediately helped the Commanders to the NFC Championship Game as a rookie.
Cam Ward perhaps offers the more relevant comparison.At Washington State in 2023, Ward displayed the big arm and the ability to create outside the pocket. But he could also lock onto his first read, hold the ball too long, leave clean pockets and force unnecessary throws. Sound familiar?After transferring to Miami for his fifth season, Ward was more comfortable working through reads, playing on time and managing pressure. His passing grade climbed from 77.5 to 91.7, while his pressure-to-sack rate improved by nine percentage points.His First-Round Readiness Score (FRED), which measures how closely a quarterback's college resume resembles previous first-round picks, jumped from 6.8 before that season to 49.3. For context, 50 represents the average first-round resume. Ward was the No. 1 overall pick in 2025.
But there's another side to his story. As I wrote recently about Ward and the Titans, through 22 NFL starts, he ranks tied for 51st in EPA per dropback among 56 first-round quarterbacks who had as many starts in their first three seasons. His 5.8 yards per attempt ranks 52nd.The familiar concerns -- holding the ball and passing up easier throws -- have followed him to the NFL. It's a reminder that another college season can turn a player into QB1 without necessarily making him a successful NFL starter.Bo Nix is another example. He entered his fifth season with 47 starts, improved his passing grade from 79.2 to 92.7 and went 12th overall in 2024. His first two NFL seasons were encouraging, although he's struggled to begin 2026.
How much did another season change things?QBStarts before final year*PFF passing grade before → afterDraft resultJayden Daniels4379.1 → 92.0No. 2, 2024Cam Ward*25+77.5 → 91.7No. 1, 2025Bo Nix4779.2 → 92.7No. 12, 2024Spencer Rattler3064.2 → 72.5No. 150, 2024Garrett Nussmeier1481.3 → 76.4No. 249, 2026Michael Penix Jr.*3088.1 → 90.5No. 8, 2024*Ward's total excludes earlier FCS experience. Penix Jr. returned for a sixth season.When more experience isn't always enoughOf course, returning to school guarantees nothing, as Garrett Nussmeier can attest. After throwing for more than 4,000 yards in 2024, he returned to LSU with just 14 career starts and legitimate first-round buzz. Instead, injuries and inconsistent play derailed his fifth season, and the quarterback once considered QB1 fell all the way to the seventh round, going 249th overall, eight picks from Mr. Irrelevant.Spencer Rattler is another cautionary example. Like Manning, he had outstanding arm talent but struggled with the must-haves that separate franchise QBs from NFL backups. Rattler improved in some areas during his fifth season at South Carolina, and I had a third-round grade on him heading into the 2024 draft, but the league viewed him as a Day 3 pick and he wasn't selected until the fifth round.Carson Beck is another example, but for a different reason. After a disappointing final season at Georgia in 2024, Beck transferred to Miami and was a much better quarterback in 2025. He was more confident, more decisive and had greater command of the offense. As I wrote following his pro day, he also became a better leader, helping Miami to the national title game while breathing new life into his NFL Draft stock. QB1 heading into that 2024 season, Beck was considered a Day 3 prospect months later, only to work himself back into the mix this spring, where he went 65th overall.The takeaway? Another year in college can make a quarterback better – but it's a two-way street. Daniels and Beck made the most of their additional seasons, while Nussmeier watched his draft stock implode. And as we're seeing with Ward, just because you're the No. 1 overall pick doesn't promise success in the NFL.So what would a fifth year mean for Arch?At 22, with just 20 starts, Manning still has room to develop. And historical examples suggest there's no reason to assume development stops after four years of college.But there's a difference between getting better and becoming the next great Manning. Arch can already make the spectacular throws – we watch it every week. But for NFL teams, it's about what it's always been about, and what former NFL quarterback and CBS Sports colleague Danny Kanell talked about recently:"Ninety percent of playing quarterback is making boring decisions, but making the right decisions, making the right reads, getting in the right protection, getting the right run plays. And then the 10% is what makes guys super special," Kanell said. "When the play breaks down, they get outside the pocket or they take the big shot … and Arch at times has had some of those wow plays."The problem that I've had with him is the 90% that he should be just delivering it at this point. Last year he had an excuse as the first-year starter. … He's been at Texas a few years. He's been able to learn the system; he should know it inside and out. They went out and got him the best wide receiver in the transfer portal in Cam Coleman, who's a stud. They got him two running backs, they got him all these pieces so that he should be putting up monster numbers and he should be performing much better, but he's not."Another 12-15 starts could absolutely give Manning the opportunity to show that growth. It could also provide evaluators with more evidence that he is who he is. And maybe all of this is moot; maybe Manning puts it all together over the next two months, and we all agree he's one of the best players in the draft class. It's possible, sure, but it seems more likely that he'll run it back one more time. And if Manning does return, the historical evidence offers a clear lesson: Being 23 years old with some 40 college starts won't prevent him from becoming a top-five pick. What matters is whether another season can make those flashes of brilliance the rule rather than the exception.

        ESPN reported Wednesday that Ashton Jeanty has been bothered by an ankle injury since the preseason and is now dealing with a foot injury. The report said the Raiders "have internally discussed giving Jeanty a week off to heal at some point." But that's not happening in Week 6 against Buffalo."He's playing," Klint Kubiak said Wednesday, adding that Jeanty is starting to "feel a lot better."Jeanty had a rough game in Week 5 at New England with 10 carries for 27 yards and three catches for 50 yards on six targets. He's yet to score a rushing touchdown this season, but he has scored at least 12.3 PPR points in three of five games. His work in the passing game has saved his production with at least three receptions in every outing and four games with at least 37 receiving yards. He's also caught two touchdowns.
I'm still starting Jeanty in the majority of leagues, but he's just a No. 2 Fantasy running back heading into Week 6 against the Bills. It's a great matchup since Buffalo is No. 2 in most Fantasy points allowed to opposing running backs, and six guys have already scored at least 13.7 PPR points against this defense.Hopefully, Jeanty will follow suit and have a strong performance. More importantly, we want him to stay healthy and not miss any games.
It's not a bad idea to stash Mike Washington Jr. (77 percent rostered on CBS Sports) in case the ESPN report is right, and the Raiders do give Jeanty a week off to heal. But, as Kubiak said, he's playing against Buffalo -- and you should start him in all leagues.

Earlier this week, Cheryl Reeve was named the Executive of the Year and Nneka Ogwumike won the Sportsmanship Award
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:40 pm ET
